definition: Antiqua et nova (Latin for 'Ancient and new') is a doctrinal note of the Catholic Church co-issued by the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith and the Dicastery for Culture and Education in January 2025.
details: It addresses the "relationship between artificial intelligence [AI] and human intelligence" and offers reflections on the "anthropological and ethical challenges raised by AI".

explainer.lead: Antiqua et nova is a January 2025 Catholic doctrinal note about how AI should relate to human intelligence. Its bottom line is simple: AI should help people think and act, not replace them. That rule shapes its warnings about schools, work, warfare, surveillance, false information, environmental costs, and concentrated corporate power.

tiers.eli5: Think of AI as a very quick helper, not a new person in charge. This Church note says the helper may give feedback or handle tasks, but people should keep thinking and deciding. It also asks adults to watch for spying, fake pictures and videos, harm to workers, weapons acting on their own, and the water and energy used by AI hardware.
tiers.practitioner: An engineer can use the note as an ethical review checklist when designing or assessing AI in education, work, health, relationships, economic settings, or warfare. For each feature, examine where human judgment remains, then check for deskilling, surveillance, loss of critical thinking, deceptive content, privacy risks, and water and energy costs. A key pitfall is treating automation as acceptable merely because it works: the note rejects replacing human intelligence and calls lethal weapons without direct human intervention or control a grave ethical concern.
tiers.paperLevel: Antiqua et nova is a 30-page, 117-paragraph doctrinal note co-issued by the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith and the Dicastery for Culture and Education. Its normative conclusion can be stated as: AI must complement, rather than replace, human intelligence. It provides anthropological and ethical analysis across six domains rather than a model, metric, or implementation, with particular attention to labor, education, lethal autonomy, surveillance, false information, environmental costs, and technocratic power.

explainer.example: A student asks an AI system for an instant critique of an essay, then revises it while continuing to practice reasoning and writing; the note cautiously allows this kind of prudent assistance. If the student instead lets the system do the thinking and stops developing critical-thinking skills, the same classroom practice illustrates its warning.

usedIn.name: Education
usedIn.detail: Weighs prudent use of instant AI critiques against the risk that students fail to develop critical thinking.

usedIn.name: Work
usedIn.detail: Examines deskilling, harsh repetitive labor, and increased surveillance of workers.

usedIn.name: Warfare
usedIn.detail: Treats autonomous lethal weapons without direct human intervention or control as a grave ethical concern.

usedIn.name: Information and privacy
usedIn.detail: Addresses deepfakes, AI-generated false information, surveillance, and matters of conscience disclosed to chat models.

explainer.intuition: The central test is whether an AI system complements human intelligence or displaces it. The note uses that test to connect individual choices with wider effects on workers, students, privacy, the environment, and democratic society.
howItWorks: Start with the relationship between artificial and human intelligence.
Examine opportunities and challenges in education, economy, work, health, relationships, and war.
Identify harms such as deskilling, surveillance, false information, and resource consumption.
Check who retains judgment, intervention, and control.
Reject uses that replace human intelligence rather than complement it.
explainer.whyItMatters: The note argues that AI choices are not only technical: they can reshape work, learning, warfare, privacy, the environment, and political power. Its strongest warning is that replacing human intelligence would enslave humanity and make AI a substitute for God.
misconceptions: It is not a blanket rejection of AI; the note discusses opportunities and cautiously allows prudent uses such as instant critiques.
Its concerns go beyond inaccurate outputs to include labor, surveillance, environmental costs, and corporate influence.
It does not present autonomous lethal weapons without direct human intervention or control as ethically neutral.

nodes.label: Six domains
nodes.note: Education, economy, work, health, relationships, war

diagram.caption: The note moves from examining AI uses and their domain-specific risks to its conclusion that AI must complement human intelligence.
